what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1972?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1972 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (132 pages) was searched for wage, gross, earnings and payroll and found only the Personnel Committee's pay SCALES (p15-16 proposed schedules; the voted schedule on p71), aggregates in the Treasurer's payments (p51-54 departmental lines such as `Police Department 80,486.40`) and in the accountant's schedule (p58 `Salaries & Wages 44,787.08` under the Police Department), payroll DEDUCTIONS held for others (p48, p53) and `EARNINGS RECEIVED DURING 1972` on two school accounts (p127-128), which are state reimbursements and not pay (sources/data/report-tables/1972/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1972 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates as VOTED in March 1972?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1972 report prints the Personnel Committee's PROPOSED schedules for March 1973 and March 1974 (p15-16, landed in `report-proposed-salary-schedule`) and the schedule voted on March 4, 1972 with its exceptions (p71 Article 3), but p71 was not sent for tables (its figures print no dollar sign, so the page read as holding fewer than three money figures) and the proposed schedules are not what was paid; searched for classification, salary schedule, step and grade (sources/data/report-tables/1972/). — closes: the Personnel Board's Classification and Salary Schedule dated March 4, 1972, as voted under Article 3 (p71), read from the page.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in calendar 1972, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1972 report prints the revolving funds' closing balances only (p44 `Revolving Funds: School Lunch 6,214.70; School Athletics .04`), the school lunch and athletic accounts inside the School Committee's report (p123, p128) and the appropriation-balance lines of the accountant's schedule (p56-67 marks `Rcts`, `RS`); no schedule of funds with receipts and disbursements was found in the text (searched: special revenue, revolving, fund, receipts reserved; sources/data/report-tables/1972/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1972 ledger of revolving and special funds.

what: What was appropriated for capital projects in 1972 and how much of it remained at the close?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a separate capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1972 report prints no such schedule: the closing balances of project appropriations appear as lines under `Appropriation Balances` on the balance sheet (p44, from `Permanent Building Committee 954.85` to `Construct/Equip Middle School 23,496.13`) and the special articles voted are listed on p73; searched for capital project, capital improvement and capital outlay (sources/data/report-tables/1972/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1972 schedule of appropriations carried forward by article.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1972?
why: `report-valuation` holds valuation and tax history from the 2000-2010 reports. The 1972 report prints the total valuation in prose (p8: real estate $49,847,600, personal property $2,180,490, total $52,028,090, tax rate $46.00, $33.00 in 1970; p2 lists the same two figures in the NOT LANDED facts table) and the overlay lines on the balance sheet (p45), but no table of valuation by class, levy or new growth was found (searched: valuation, tax rate, levy, overlay, assessed; sources/data/report-tables/1972/). — closes: the Board of Assessors' 1972 tax rate recapitulation (the State's form for the tax rate).

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1972, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1972 report prints the Inspector of Weights and Measures' work in prose (p26: 127 devices inspected, 124 sealed, one pump and two scales condemned), the `Sealing Fees 324.10` receipt (p49) and the budget lines `Inspector of Weights & Measures 765.00` (p72) and 730.25 paid (p51); no table of devices by type with fees was found (searched: sealer, weights and measures, devices, sealing; sources/data/report-tables/1972/). — closes: the Inspector of Weights and Measures' 1972 annual report to the Town, by device type.
